proof_summary: Assuming the first asserted identity makes the shifted values \(u_k=a(3773+k)+1\) satisfy the Fibonacci recurrence; initial-value and modular Fibonacci computations modulo \(p=195318521017\) show that for \(k=249580073233\), \(u_k=u_{k+1}=1\), so \(p\) divides both corresponding consecutive terms. Their gcd is therefore \(g\ge2\); writing their sum as \(gq\) gives \(q\ge2\), while the defining recurrence and the asserted identity would force \(g+q=1+gq\), which is impossible for \(g,q\ge2\).
